We've added a Pansun backup that guarantees you receive all the Pansuns you had earned until that point in the match if you suffer a disconnection at some point.

We've made the online system a bit more tolerant to errors, so that it will not immediately cause a disconnection upon finding an issue. Right now the disconnection is automatically happening, even with errors that are pretty harmless and don't interfere in the successful completion of a match. This will hopefully allow everyone to suffer less disconnections, and make the Swarm experience a bit more enjoyable.

We've removed the added requirements for the Reanimation Gear kit to appear in your pool, which were that you needed to have the Revive node active in that Temtem's skill tree. You'll now be offered this Gear even if you don't have that Skill Tree node unlocked, making Blockade+ easier to achieve.

We've heard your feedback on how hard it is to go from being able to use all the Pansuns earned to only being able to use linked Pansuns on Prestige level 1. To try to offset this initial jump into hardcore content, we've added a set amount of linked Pansuns to each Temtem when you unlock its first Prestige Level.

This amount will be different for each Temtem: the more expensive the Tem's Skill Tree is, the bigger the bonus will be. As a rule of thumb, it will give enough Pansuns to cover the unlocking of approximately 20% of the full Skill Tree on Prestige Level 1.

The bonus will apply retroactively to everyone who has reached Prestige Level 1 on any Temtem, and will be applied to each Tem. This bonus will only take effect upon unlocking the first Prestige Level, and won't be granted for further Prestige Levels.
Thanks for sharing your feedback and suggestions with us! Let's keep building a better Temtem: Swarm together.

items.text: Hello, Tamers! We come back with another update to try and keep the major bugs under control, which are: being locked in the level-up screen and the disconnections at minute 20. For full transparency, we've added some safe checks in order to avoid or correct the bug situations, but since we still haven't managed to internally reproduce them, we can't be 100% sure the safe checks work as intended. We'll monitor your information closely, and remember that if you find any issue there's a helpful guide on how to report them here.
All platforms
Fixed the softlock for guest players if the host closed the lobby while the guest was in any Skill Tree menu.
PS5
Fixed getting stuck when joining a co-op lobby through an invite of through PSN's services.
Fixed public lobbies becoming private the moment we select an Arena to play.
Fixed private lobbies becoming public ones if we turned on the Share Experience setting.
We apologize again for all the trouble. Thanks for being patient with us while we fix it.

Hello, Tamers! This patch has been made to correct some bugs, but also to add new logs that might give us more information and insight into the two major bugs that we're unable to reproduce internally. We're well aware they're pretty consistent across the community, but so far we haven't been able to reproduce them internally, even when they're so pervasive for you, our players.

We hope the logs will help us identify the problem at last, but if you're playing on PC and encounter any of these issues, please don't close the game, and get your logs from the following folder: (%userprofile%\AppData\LocalLow\Crema\TemtemSwarm)

After you've secured the logs, and before you close the game, please share them with us on our Discord bug forum, or send them to support@cremagames.com with all the info you can gather from the match and the issue.
We're really sorry for the inconveniences, and thank you for your patience.
All platforms

items.text: We apologize for the inconveniences, and for requesting your help at a time like this. Let's hope you can enjoy Swarm as it was meant to be soon!
Welcome to patch 1.0, the patch where we leave Early Access, the patch that unlocks everything, rounds everything up, and allows you to enjoy Temtem: Swarm to the fullest!
Today is also Temtem: Swarm's launch on PS5! We hope PlayStation 5 players will have a blast playing Swarm, and that Nintendo Switch players can join us very soon!
Two new playable Temtem: Venx and Chromeon.
Let's start with the Neutral cutie with the split evolutionary path! Venx, and by extension Venmet and Vental, can now be playable in Temtem: Swarm.
Venx has two possible evolutions: a mental one, called Vental, and a Melee one, called Venmet.

Once Venx levels up enough to evolve, the level-up screen will give you the option to choose whether you want to continue playing with Vental or Venmet. Although they share a trait, they have very different stats, access to different Technique pools, and a unique Ultimate each.

You can also choose not to evolve Venx, like with every other playable Tem, by blocking the evolution perk or ignoring it forever (do keep in mind that the evolution slot will always block a Synergy one!)
Its Trait grants bonuses to their final forms depending on how long you postpone the evolution!
And of course, the Digital marvel that is Chromeon! Enjoy 12 Tems for the price of one!

Chromeon is a Digital Temtem with the particularity that it has an adaptive second type that can be any elemental type in Temtem: Swarm. Chromeon changes secondary type every time it uses its Ultimate, Torrent.
Its main type will always be Digital, and the secondary type will be selected at random after using Torrent. The secondary typing at the beginning of the game is also decided randomly.
Torrent, the Ultimate, has elemental variants for each elemental type. Some can apply status conditions to enemies, others apply positive buffs to Chromeon. Try them all!

Chromeon will only be offered Techniques of its current secondary typing at level up. And since it drinks from all elemental types, this gives Chromeon access to all Techniques in the game. Digital Techniques may show up at any level-up since it's its primary typing.
Its Trait increases Chromeon's Damage by 10% for each different elemental type of its equipped techs - including the ultimate.
A new Arena: welcome to The Evershifting Tower!

This miracle of digital engineering and procedural generation is the final and most challenging Arena so far. Its most notorious characteristic? It changes from run to run, so neither you nor your Tems will get a moment of peace here!

Instead of creating a set layout, as we usually do, for The Evershifting Tower we've created 150 different tiles, tiles which are then procedurally arranged at the start of every run, making for an immense number of possible layouts.
And not only the layout: the waves of enemies will also be random every time a new wave spawns, ranging from all available types plus Digital Temtem, which will always be present.
But there's more challenge to it! All enemies get one small, medium and big buff to their HP, Damage or Speed at random!
The Spots in The Evershifting Tower are also randomized, so you might get more Pansun spots or Experience spots depending on the run. The same goes for Glitches and Chest spots.

The one thing that is not randomized? The three sensational, boosted mini-bosses that give way to the proud, fearsome boss that reigns over the skies and the Evershifting Tower. Good luck against its incredible kit!
👥The Prestige System
This is an entirely new system meant to provide long-term, endgame goals for the enthusiastic Temtem: Swarm players.

Once you’ve fully maxed out a Temtem’s Skill Tree, you can reset it to unlock Prestige Level 1. As you complete the Skill Tree fully again, resetting it will grant you Prestige Level 2, and so on, up until level 10, which is the maximum Prestige Level.

Every Prestige Level you gain, starting from level 1, will add a passive bonus to that Temtem. It's different and unique to every Temtem, and it only applies to them. Every time the Prestige level increases, the bonus effects of this personal passive will improve.

The first Prestige Level will also grant a global passive, meaning it applies to every playable Temtem. Every Tem can provide a different global passive, so make sure to reach Prestige Level 1 on many Tems to power up your entire roster!
Once your Temtem is at Prestige Level 1 and onwards, it will only gain Pansuns linked to it, meaning Pansuns that can only be used on that Temtem's Skill Tree.

Their Skill Tree nodes will only accept Pansuns earned with that Temtem to be unlocked and improved. The amount of Pansuns required to reach each progressive Prestige level will increase, making every step a bit more challenging than the previous one. Give it your best!

You can reset your Prestige Level to 0 if you want to. Doing so will remove all Prestige levels, return all the linked Pansuns to the player, and reset the Skill Tree nodes to 0. This will also remove the previously earned personal and global passive buffs, but it won't remove the Luma (and Umbra) versions of the Temtem.
If you reset your Prestige Level to 0, that Temtem will go back to earning general Pansuns, which can be used on any other Temtem's Skill Tree (as long as there's no Prestige Level).
The Prestige System is also the key to unlock Lumas and Umbras. See below!
Lumas and Umbras storm the party!
Here they are, the coveted color variations of our playable Temtem! These variations don't affect gameplay, so you can freely choose which version you want to use.
Reaching Prestige Level 1, and then winning a match with that Temtem will unlock the shiny Luma version of it for you to enjoy!
Reaching Prestige Level 2, and then winning a match with that Temtem will unlock the elusive "gothic counterpart", the Umbra version.

Color variations can be chosen from the Temtem selection menu, which you can also access while in a lobby. Once you select an option, it will be saved for following games, so remember to change it before a match if you want to use a different one!

Once you unlock the first Luma and Umbra version of a Temtem, any of them, enemies will have a chance of spawning Luma or Umbra. All enemies may appear Luma or Umbra, regardless of which Luma/Umbra you have unlocked. The rates for Luma enemies appearing are 0,12%, while the rates for Umbra enemies are 0,08%.

The Luma and Umbra enemies' stats will remain unchanged, but they will drop x3 or x6 times the experience they normally would, respectively. As a bonus, Luma enemies will drop an extra Reroll pickup, while Umbra enemies drop an extra Block pickup.
This applies to all enemies except bosses, mini-bosses, powerful Tems, and the Hazrat from the "Catch the Hazrat" spot.
The Tempedia has been added:
All the information about Temtem: Swarm, at the tip of your fingers: the Tempedia is a recollection of all the elements of the game where Tamers can find answers to all their questions.
It contains information on:

Techniques: Description, synergy and the Gear required for it, and whether the player has used it or not, and won a match with it or not. These can appear as Locked or Unlocked depending on having completed the associated Kudos, but it will show you which Kudo you need to complete to unlock it.

Gears: Description, whether the player has used it or not, and won a match with it or not. These can appear as Locked or Unlocked depending on having completed the associated Kudos, but it will show you which Kudo you need to complete to unlock it.
Glitches (only accessible once the player has picked up a Glitch during a match): Effects of each, and whether the player has used it or not, and won a match with it or not.
Pickups: Shows a description of each available pickup.

Arenas: You can see whether the player has completed them or not, the maximum Hacking Level in a successful run, which Temtem defeated the boss, and whether it happened on the maximum Hacking Level possible, and longest time spent in a run on the Arena, for Endless mode and for normal matches. An extra menu can be accessed once the Arena is unlocked to see the primary types in the Arena, better and worse types to use there, and a list of all enemies found in the Arena.

Tems: divided into two categories, the first one shows the playable Tems and their details, including but not limited to their types, evolutions, Ultimates, Traits, Prestige Levels, matches played and won, best time during a match, and much more. These can appear as Locked or Unlocked depending on whether you have played a match with them.: The second category covers the Temtem enemies and their details, including but not limited to their types, stats, behaviors and movement, maps where they can be found, number defeated by the player, and more. These can appear as Locked or Unlocked, depending on whether you have defeated one Temtem of that species before.
Glossary: Lists all the variables in the game, with their corresponding icons and a description showing what they do. Variables include all the stats, status condition effects, types, and more.
👥Match history: Lists the last 10 matches played.
The Tempedia can be accessed from the Main Menu.
Crossplay has been added! Enjoy playing with PC and PS5 players for now, and with Nintendo Switch players in the future!
We've added 3 new Hacking modifiers.
Level up Perks are chosen randomly, although it won't swap Techniques or Gears once all slots are full.
Every 15 levels, a random equipped Gear is destroyed.
Every 15 levels, a random equipped Technique is destroyed, unless you only have one Tech. It won't delete a Tech if it's your only damaging Technique equipped.
The maximum Hacking level has been raised to 15! Give it your best ;)
We've added 6 new interesting Glitches to make your runs spicier.
Effective damage deals 60% more damage, but all other damage deals 20% less damage
Increases your damage by 100%, but reduces it by 1 for every 100 meters traveled.
Increases your max HP by 50%, but you lose one random Tech.
Increases your damage at max HP by 65%, but reduces your max HP by 25%.
Status conditions can now deal critical damage, but your Armor is reduced by 30%.
When healing, deal 200% of the heal as damage to all enemies, but your HP recovery is reduced a 100%.

Rerolls, Blocks and Snoozes have been added as pickup items that can be found in boxes or chests across the map, or as a super rare drop by Luma, Umbra or Powerful Tems. These will only start appearing after you've unlocked the Block Skill Tree node for any Temtem.
We've added 218 new Kudos. Enjoy completing them all!
We've added 32 new Steam Achievements.
We've created some new thrilling OST pieces for the new Arena and its boss! The OST is now completed, and you can find it on all streaming platforms.

Temtem: Swarm now has credits! You'll be able to see them once you defeat the Evershifting Tower boss for the first time, before you get to the End of Run screen. You can also choose to skip the credits, but that would make our teams sad. Thank you for supporting us and following along during the Early Access period.
👥Your Ultimate will instantly recharge after evolution, so you can enjoy your evolution with a bang!
👥There's now a chance to get better health items or Pansun items upon level up, and the Luck stat of your Temtem improves it!
We've made a handful of improvements to improve performance and lower memory consumption.
When exchanging an equipped Technique for another, the new Tech will be two levels lower than the exchanged one instead of being at Level 1.
When exchanging an equipped Gear for another, the new Gear will have its level assigned depending on the rarity of the Gears switched.
Since the maximum Hacking Level has been raised to 15, players will increase 2 ➜ 3 steps of the bar after successfully completing a match.
No more Skill Tree caps! Since all Skill Trees can be completed now, all references to the caps have been removed.
👥We've added a new flair to Kudos sections that are 100% completed.
We've slightly reduced the TemCard size in the Tem Selector menu so that all playable Tems fit and you don't have to scroll!
We've removed the green and red borders on Techs in the Pause menu, so you can clearly see which Tech you're hovering over or selecting.
We've added icons to some Stats that didn't have one before.
We've made some improvements and corrections to the UI.
General
👥Dash damage now properly escalates with Temtem damage, taking into account any Stat improvement instead of using only the base damage.
The armor formula has been adjusted:
There is no longer an armor cap (although for gameplay reasons you cannot reach 100% Armor).
Every armor point over 99, which used to be the cap, will now be added as 0.003% damage reduction, making it possible to reach 99.99% damage reduction.

Critical Probability and Critical Damage have been adjusted in all damaging Techniques so all of them have the same values: 5% Critical Probability and 50% Critical Damage. Techniques with set Critical Probabily are exempt from this adjustment.

items.text: Welcome to the patch notes! If you're more of a visual learner, check out patch 0.8's launch trailer if you haven't yet!
A new Arena: Welcome to the Pansun!
Stand in the glowing plates of the Pansun and face all its mysteries in the new Temtem: Swarm arena.
A new zone to explore, with new Landmarks closely based on its Temtem counterpart, and enemies of the Fire, Earth and Crystal type.
Two new mini-bosses and an imposing new boss, a certain ruler of the cosmos.
New soundtrack pieces to bop to in this galactic environment!
New playable character: Pycko and Drakash!
This Earth/Fire duo are here to bring chaos and fun to your playtime!

With a fantastically chaotic Trait that burns and gives Pycko a momentary Speed boost upon contact with an enemy, and a new base attack that has a new, double-sided targetting, they're sure to make the delights of players who love to zoom around wreaking havoc.
👥The great Kudos revival!
We have revamped and redone the Kudos menu to be much simpler and easier to navigate.
Instead of the previous hexagon-ladden screen, you can now see all your Kudos in one neat, easy-to-scroll list.
The Kudos are still divided in categories and subcategories, the same ones used previously.
This change came forth from all your suggestions and feedback on the previous Kudos map. Thanks for sharing your opinions with us, and please keep doing so in the future!
More information in each Kudo.
We've changed all Kudos to include the information to unlock them right off the bat, except any info that might be a spoiler to new players.
You will also be able to see which Kudo goes with which Skill Tree Node directly from each Skill Tree.

Kudos are now shown in four simple states: coming soon (wait for the next update), spoiler-covered (we'll give you the info but without spoilers), unlocked (you've unlocked this one and are already making progress) and completed (you're done!).
👥In-game tracking for Kudos, too!
You can now access a mini Kudos menu to review the Kudos that are available for you to complete then and there.
It's tailored to show you the Kudos associated with the Tem you're using and the Arena you're playing in.
This is another frequent community request and we're happy to deliver. Keep a close eye on your progression right from the comfort of your match!

As an extra, we have also moved some Kudos to a most fitting category. The best example would be that Kudos like "Deal x damage with y Technique" have been moved to the part of the map where said Technique is unlocked, to minimize confusion.
👥New Setting: Technique opacity.
We've added a new slider in the Settings menu that lets you customize the opacity of the player Techniques. Choose how intense or how subtle you want the VFX in your matches be!

To add the cherry on top, you will also see your co-op partners' Techniques in the same opacity you have set for yourself. Take this practical example: if player A has set their opacity to 25%, they will see player B's Techniques at 25% opacity; if player B has set their opacity to 72%, they will see player A's Techniques at 72% opacity. Control your screen all the way!

Although we've been listening to your feedback and manually adjusting some Techniques to improve visibility, it was clear that a broader step had to be taken, so we're giving you complete choice over Technique transparency. We hope this change will alleviate most of the issues our players have with visibility, but we'll still be alert to take any extra measure or work on it if need be.
A new Stat: Dodge.
Dodge symbolizes the chance a player has of dodging any instance of damage.
To start dodging, please first unlock the pertinent Skill Tree Node for all the Tems you want to be dodging with.
Dodge covers all damage, including proyectiles, attacks, damage areas, minibosses' and bosses' kits, etc.
👥Cursor customization!
Both the in-game cursor and the aiming pointer can now be customized in two different ways: shape and size.
Choose from a variety of shapes and colors in the shape selector and pick the one that's best for you.
Once you have your shape decided, choose from a range of sizes, from small to big, until your cursor is just perfect.

This feature, which is also community-rquested, is also framed as part of our efforts to make visibility in Temtem: Swarm better for everyone. We hope you will all find a cursor you like, or at least one you don't lose track of during the fray!
New Hacking modifiers!

Add more spice to your challenge with 5 new Hacking level modifiers that you can mix and match during the Hacking Mode selector: Pick-ups that disappear after a bit, extra mini-Bosses, and enemies that have an increasable chance of exploding, leaving waste pools behind or being shielded. Have fun!
New Gears!
Spyglass.
This new Gear increases the damage that enemies with any Status condition receive. Perfect for the new playable Tem!
Kaleidotonic
This new Gear increases the damage dealt by Status Conditions. Also perfect for the new evo line!
7 new Glitches to delight our challenge-oriented players.
New Dash tutorial!
This tutorial will pop up for new players who have Unlocked Oree but haven't unlocked the Kudo that allows other Tems to have a Dash node in the Skill Tree.
Many new players wonder how to get the Dash for other Tems that aren't Oree, who comes with a built in Dash. This tutorial should help with that!

To pair up with this change, we've adjusted it so if you have an Oree egg among other eggs, the Oree egg will always be the one to hatch first. That way we can introduce the Dash and the new Dash tutorial to new players as soon as possible.
Returning pickup: Mayhem Drive.
All fun, no cooldowns! This pickup causes your Tem to spam all their Techs without any cooldown for five seconds.
We're aware that Mayhem Drive found its way into the game on patch 0.7
New Steam achievements to complete!
👥We've made some improvements and QoL changes to the Pause menu:
You can now see the interactions between Perks by hovering over any Perk. This means which Gears affect what Techniques, and vice versa.
We've added text to the Pause buttons so that it's easier to identify what each of them does.
You can now see your Temtem's Trait description in the Pause menu.
Use your right-click button to leave or exit any menu!
It will now work like the ESC button for all UIs.

👥Floor is lava has gotten further improvements to better its visibility with a new upwards VFX, and a much bigger ball. We hope this change, along with the change in Technique opacity, will make this spot less troublesome for you!
👥We've created a distinction on the Synergy menu during a match to differentiate between unlocked and undiscovered Synergies.
Synergies that you haven't unlocked yet (you haven't found the right Kudo nor have you leveled up the base Technique to level 5) show with a lock symbol.
Synergies that you haven't discovered yet (you've completed the Kudo, but you've never used this Synergy and don't know the recipe yet) now show with an interrogation mark.
👥We've added map markers for pick-up items, just like the ones fruits have. This includes speed Boots, invincible Armor, chips, etc.
If you're at full health but had turned on the setting to autoselect a healing item upon level up, the healing item will now spawn in the map as a pick-up.
The Glitches tab will now be hidden in the End of the Run screen if we haven't picked any Glitch during the match.
We've reworked the Tem selector in the Skill Trees so that it would match the pre-game one.
We've reviewed all the UI bits across Temtem: Swarm to improve them and make sure they were cohesive and accurate.
We've made some extra performance adjustments and UX improvements to the new Kudos section so that it's smooth to navigate.
We've added Steam timeline markers for the new mini-bosses and boss.
General
Dash Damage now scales based on the playable Temtem's damage.
As opposed to being a fixed number, damage will now be dynamic and tied to the player's Damage.
In-game descriptions of Skills have been adjusted following this change.
Damage numbers shown in the End of the Run screen have been adjusted and will now only show the damage used to defeat the enemy Tem.

Before, the whole damage dealt by the Technique was counted, even if only a 10% of that had already defeated the enemy Tem. This was causing visible imbalance between Techs that hit bluntly and Techs that deal damage through Status Conditions, because the latter only ever user as much damage as it was needed to defeat the enemy.
To equalize this across the board on the EoR screen, the damage numbers shown will be those used to defeat the enemy, but not the surplus.
All Skill Trees' optional caps have been uncapped further.

items.text: The Temtem: Swarm demo is back!
You'll be able to play the Cipanku arena with Platypet, Smazee and Oree.
Any progress you make in the demo will transfer to the full game when you purchase it.
Demo players are able to play with players from the full version, as long as they're playing on the Arenas available in the Demo and without Challenge Modes.
If your friends are on the fence about picking it up, please let them know they can now try the game entirely for free!
We're introducing 4 new Neutral Techniques that can be used by all Tems.
They're Rotten Zone, Rainbow Guard, Expanding Force and Darkness.
Each of these also has a synergy associated.
👥On top of this, all Temtem have gained access to previously-existing Neutral Techs.
This will effectively duplicate the Tech Pools of all Temtem, and should help make runs more unique with the broader range of Techs.
We've added connection indicators to lobbies.
We already had them on the lobby explorer, but now you'll also be able to see the strength of your connection with the host even in private lobbies.
Created new Kudos for the new Neutral Techniques.
We've added a little invulnerability time after levelling up and choosing a perk, similar to the one we get after evolving.
👥We've added a new option for players with a full build to auto-select their perks.
When your build is full, the next level up will show you a checkbox to auto-select either Pansuns or health items.
Once you make your choice it will stay that way until the end of the match.
👥Likewise, we've introduced a setting to skip the animation and automatically get all rewards out of chests for players who have a full build.
Like with Perks, players will need to check a box while picking a chest so the change can be applied on all chests moving forwards.
Pickable items, like the speed boots, Magnets or the invulnerability shield, will spawn on the map so the player can pick them up when they desire.
We've added a new pop-up the first time you visit the Skill Tree of a newly unlocked Temtem.
It will display the info on how many Linked Pansuns you have in that Skill Tree.
Linked Pansuns are Pansuns that can only be spent in that particular Skill Tree. They are used first when upgrading Skill Tree Nodes.
👥We've focused a lot of efforts in this patch on tackling the issues with pool dilution:
To start with, we've increased the chance of getting perks that synergize with any of your equipped perks.
You must have the synergy unlocked for this to happen. Make sure you complete many Kudos to unlock everything!
We have further lowered the chance of perks that you don't select from appearing in further level ups.
We've increased the chances of getting 4 perk slots when we have a full build.
This was previously only based on the Luck skill, but now we have added a 40% base bonus to it.
With enough Luck skill, the possibilty can grow to reach a 100% chance.
The base probability of Techs showing on the level up when the player has all their Tech slots filled has been reduced to a 20%, so the possibility of being offered a Gear goes up to 80%.
We have increased the number of blocks, rerolls and snoozes to 5 each.
We have set some measures to prevent and control the issue causing players who had suffered a crash to experience corrupt save files.
We'll still be closely monitoring to ensure swift action if something comes up.
We've take some measures to improve and prevent performance issues on Hasty and Endless Mode,
We've given a performance review pass to Swarm enemies and fixed a past mishap, which will improve performance across the board.
We've set a soft cap on the amount of Swarm enemies shown on screen.
Undefeated enemies that would normally re-spawn around the player character will now de-spawn if the cap has been reached.
This only affects normal Swarm enemies, and doesn't affect bosses, mini-bosses or powerful enemies.
👥We have given map visibility a complete review pass:
We've shrunken or moved map elements, such as rocks on the borders of the Arenas.
We've added transparency to props and elements that are scattered around the map, so that if players come close to them they can still see through.
With this we hope to improve the visibility players have during their runs, and to prevent the player character from disappearing behind obstacles.
We've added a blinking effect to the markers to the No Hit and Art Restoration spots so they're easier to complete.
We're making changes to prevent the HUD being hidden in the Settings for returning players.
All HUDs will now be toggled ON by default, but you can turn them off in the Settings Menu.
If you had set your HUD off on Settings, you will need to redo this again after this patch. Apologies for the inconveniences.
We've increased the width of the Temtem selection menu box so that you have to scroll less.
We've removed the check symbol on the Swarm map selection to avoid confusion.
We've greatly increased the amount of Pansuns that newly unlocked Tems receive.
If you had already unlocked said Tems, you'll get the extra Pansuns when you log in.
These Pansuns will be tied to the Temtem you receive them on and will only be usable in that Temtem's Skill Tree.
You can see the change for each Temtem lower below.
This change will drastically improve the grind required to enjoy a new Temtem. Go ahead and give them all a try!
We've adjusted the Pansuns received from rejecting a Glitch in Co-op so they take into account the number of players in the run.
We've reworked Experience Chests so that they better adapt to the momentum of the match.
This means the further you're in a match, the more experience these chests will drop.
From minute 15 onwards, the experience rewards already overcome the maximum reward you could get before.
👥We've corrected the damage multiplier when using a technique that's both effective and ineffective against a double-type Temtem.
It was previously 0.91, and it's now 1, as they cancel each other's typing advantage and disadvantage.

Players can add and remove Hacking Modifiers at will, crafting a unique experience every time, perfectly catered to their liking.
Adding Hacking Modifiers will increase the Hacking level: the higher the Hacking level is, the more your rewards will multiply!

You will find there’s an initial limit to the Hacking level you can set for an Arena: clear the Arena in that Hacking level to unlock further Hacking levels, and so on! You won’t be able to save your Hacking configuration if you’re over your current limit.
There are currently 10 available modifiers that you can mix and match, from simple ones, like lowering your Health or increasing the Swarm’s health, to complex ones likes Endless and Hasty.
Endless: Play infinite cycles of waves after waves! Only your own ability will determine how far you get. Each wave will be tougher than the one before, so stay on your toes!
Hasty: Crank up that speed! The Hasty modifier propels the match’s timer, making enemies appear faster which in turn snowballs into crazy runs with crazy speed.
To unlock Hacking levels for an Arena, you must first defeat the Arena boss in less than 40 seconds!
Only the host of a match can adjust and save Hacking modifiers in a lobby.
The reward modifiers for the Hacking Levels also account for each Arena’s own Pansun multiplier, which means you’ll earn even more Pansuns from playing Hacking Modes on difficult Arenas.

Available, public lobbies are now shown in a list with all their information, and players can choose to join the one they prefer.

Apart from the Arena, chosen Tem, shared EXP or not, etc, the lobbies will now display they quality of the connection between you and the host of that match, letting you choose the ones that will ensure better latency and better performance.
You won’t be able to see public lobbies that are too far away from you, that have chosen an Arena you haven’t unlocked yet, or that have a Hacking level over your current limit.
The list of lobbies automatically refreshes every 2 seconds.
The previous system also works, so you can still join lobbies through a code if you so desire, and create private lobbies for you and your friends
We hope this new take on lobbies is closer to what our players had in mind!

We’ve also added information about the quality of your connection through some icons on the right side of your screen at the beginning of a run.

If you see this icons at the beginning of the match, please be aware that lag can happen, and that lag can lead to issues during the run. Try looking for people you have a better connection with if this happens.
A ping system!
No voice chat? No problem! Communicate your needs to your co-op partners with the new ping system, that will let you choose from 10 preset expressions to convey different things!

The available pings are: Help!, Hello!, Thanks!, Good job!, Follow me, Need healing, Ultimate Status (which shows if your Ultimate is available or not), Confirm, Disagree and Doubt (which can be used near pick-ups and spots to ask contextualized questions, with the icon changing to represent what the question is about).
When pings happen outside of your screen they will appear like spots or pick-ups do, with the animation to really capture your eye. Pings also have a sound effect so you don’t miss any!
Please don’t try to spam pings! There is a cooldown system in place that will prevent you from using them if you overuse them. If you insist, the cooldown will become increasingly longer.
You can also mute other players’ pings from your own wheel of pings.

👥We have increased the total number of Blocks and Rerolls you can have through the Skill Tree.
We've added one more level to these two Nodes, meaning you can now get one more Block and one more Reroll per match if you level these nodes up.
We plan to keep increasing Blocks and Rerolls in the future as we continue adding new content to the game, so finding the right pieces for your build doesn't get harder with more content.

We're aware of the concerns surrounding the diluting of the pool as we add, and players unlock, new perks. We've got a couple of improvements for it that will be included in patch 0.7, but in the meantime we believe increasing Blocks and Rerolls definitely helps.
👥You can now select if you want to create a public or private lobby right from the Lobby creation screen.

👥We've added varying percentages of armor to Eggs:
This will make the Egg more resistant and durable across all maps, but the Eggs will have different armor percentages depending on the map.
Harder maps or maps that are completed later down the row will have a more protected and resistant Eggs to combat the increase in difficulty.
We've adjusted the way the Pansuns and exp magnets work:
Instead of pulling in all the pieces scattered across the map onto your character all at once, we've now set a speed for pieces that will take into account how far from you they are.
This way you will first receive the ones closer to you, and so on, as in a scale.
We've adjusted the description of Traits and Ultimate Techniques so it shows a dynamic number calculated taking into account the upgrades on the Skill Tree
We've adjusted the way upgrades to Techs and Gears appear when you receive them from a reward chest.
It will no longer show the description for said Gear or Tech.
Instead, it'll display only the stat changes that are taking place with the upgrade.

Max HP 9999
Speed 25
Critical Probability 100
To clarify, this cap will never affect permanent upgrades, like Gears or Skill Tree increases.
It will only ever act when a player concatenates a series of temporal effects (like the speed boost from Gotta Go Fast!).
We've put these in place to prevent bugs and issues, but it won't require anything from players and you can play normally!
👥We have reduced the time required to complete a Capture Spot from 5 to 3 minutes.

Following your feedback on how complicated the Spot was with the 5 minute mark, and given it's a really important Spot that we want everyone to be able to complete, we've lowered the time requirement for it.
We've added distance and duration modifiers to Art Restoration based on the amount of players in the group.
The more players, the farther the pieces will go, and the less time you'll have to pick them up
We wanted to add a little extra challenge to this Spot in co-op, as it was too easy in its previous state.
We've made adjustments to Gotta Go Fast! to make sure the rings always prioritize appearing in walking distance of the previous ring, avoiding structures and collisions.
If no suitable place is found on the first pass, the game will soften the requirements, .
Even if the ring ends up appearing in the same place as the one before, we want to make sure all players can complete this Spot.
We've made the Hazrat in Catch the Rat immune to status conditions, like powerful Tems or Bosses are.
We've slightly adjusted the prices of the Reroll and Block nodes, with the idea that we keep scaling it as more Rerolls and Blocks are added in the future.

Hello, Tamers! We have some news regarding the launch of patch 0.6 for Temtem: Swarm, which is a content update and not a polish one!

Our goal is to release patch 0.6 in the first half of March, which means we're aiming at the first or second week! With all the new content and changes to major features in this patch, we want to be optimistic, but have to keep the possibility open for delays in case something unexpected happens during this final stage of testing, polishing and re-balancing. We're not planning to go any further than the month of March, though!
We're, of course, working on a specific date, and as soon as we have it we'll provide it!

If you've been following around for a bit, you already know of two big things coming with patch 0.6: a new Arena, Omninesia, and random Matchmaking. With this new Arena you'll be able to enjoy two new playable Tems! We'll be spoiling one of them in the upcoming days, so I'd keep an eye out on our communication avenues if I were you. We're also trying out the new minimum match duration that you voted for, 20 minutes, so the experience is surely going to be different from what you've played so far!
But there's something else we've come to share spoilers for today: Spots!

Patch 0.6 comes with a handful of completely new spots, many of them suggested by the community itself! But beyond adding new Spots that players can enjoy, we've also reworked three of the old ones to make them more fun, more rewarding and/or more challenging, also following community feedback.
Want to see a very relevant spot that got changed? Peep this:

The Swarm is getting closer, Tamers! We're already working on the bug-fixing and polishing stages of patch 0.6, and we're eager to conquer these feats and present you the newest level of Temtem Swarming. You're going to love it!

items.text: We've added a backup system for save games:
Up until now, when the game detected a corrupted save game it would completely erase it so the game could be launched again. However, this has lead to players losing their progress completely.
From now on, the system will create a copy of your current save game before overwriting it, and if your save game ends up corrupted one way or another, it will offer you to return to that backup.
While some progress might still be lost in the process, it will not be all progress like it's happened up until now.

Please note that the backup isn't bulletproof. It can get corrupted, in which case the save game will be erased so you can continue playing, or it can have issues saving. That's why we always encourage you to close the game in a safe way (avoid alt+f4 or abrupt turning off of the computer), and to please share with us any crash you might experience. You can do so here.
We've reworked the in-game status pickups.
They now work similar to a Tech in the sense that the playable Temtem is the center of it, and it expands outwards in a circle, applying the status and dealing damage in waves.
The Temtem portraits are now animated across the board!
However, since this can consume more resources, we've added a setting for it in the Settings menu, so you can turn it on or off depending on your specs.
We've added a summary of dash damage to the end-of-the-run screen!
We've added a myriad of new, informative notifications for all sort of situations when trying to connect with other players.
We've made some adjustments to the way things are loaded, so you should see faster loading time, less use of resources when you're in the menu, and way less crashes upon opening the game.
The Arbury shores should now display movement!

Not being able to aim has been, without any doubt, the biggest issue we got during our Playtesting and Demo periods. We're so happy we've been able to fulfill this massive task in the short time between the Demo and the Early Access release, and we quite like the result. The current implementation should work for all kind of players since everyone's still able to just ignore aiming and keep playing as before, but better, because now those techniques will auto-aim to the closest target.

We've hugely reworked how Spots (in-game events) are spawned and positioned:
Before, spots were pre-determined in both type (Nest, Pansun Fest...) and location, leading to them being predictable and getting boring after a few runs.

Now spots will spawn randomly through the run, so each game will be different. There are a lot of rules in place so as not to swamp players with too many spots (or too few), and we hope it feels much better than before overall. We'll be listening to your reactions to this change!

We're planning a further and deeper rework on Spots, which includes reworking some of the current Spot types, creating new ones and reworking their rewards too. We'll be working on this on future patches during the Early Access period.
The new default gamepad button for using the ultimate is now LB (LT can also be used), and the button for dash is now RB (RT can be used too).
We're working on the controller and key remap feature, and we're hoping to have it relatively soon! With this you'll be able to set your keys and buttons any way you prefer.
We're really sorry about your muscle memory, but this button setting feels much nicer overall now that you need to use your second thumb in the joystick too.

At the end of the run, Pansun decimals will be rounded down to the closest number.
The Kudos menu now has a pre-selection menu, or lobby, if you will, which improves the navigation and allows players to directly zoom in into any specific Kudo group they want to check out.
We've improved the loading screen. It will now showcase the selected Temtem (or Tems when playing in a co-op party), and it will also show interesting tips or fun facts!
Techniques will now display their targeting on their little info card, so players can better know how they will behave when picked.
Improved the visibility and readability of the status conditions affecting the player.
Only the two closest healing items will be displayed as markers in the map now, in order to avoid too much clutter on screen.

Leaving a run will now go through the same flow as getting knocked-out, so doing this will get players to the end-of-run screen. This will allow you to unlock Kudos and receive the rewards gathered during the run.

We will consider this patch as a "clean slate" for balancing to work upon for future patches.

While we love to see the players' creativity in ways to farm infinitely while escaping from the boss, we don't want that to become the main way to farm Pansuns and make players feel forced to do so to improve their farming. items.text: We're so close to that coveted green checkmark! While we haven't quite reached the full "Verified" status yet, we're thrilled to share that Temtem: Swarm is officially "Playable" on Steam Deck!

That means you can dive into the chaotic world of Temtem: Swarm on your Steam Deck and have a blast on launch day! While there might be a few minor hiccups, like some tiny text or the occasional keyboard glyphs, the core gameplay experience is fantastic. Beyond those hiccups, we did get the green check for these super important pieces during the review:
All functionality is accessible when using the default controller configurations
This game’s default graphics configuration performs well on Steam Deck

That being said, we’re fully committed to making the Deck experience as perfect as possible. We're already hard at work to address the feedback from Valve and make Temtem: Swarm fully Verified in no time. We're aiming to have these fixes ready soon, and we'll be resubmitting for review as quickly as possible.

If there’s anyone on the fence because of the ‘Playable’ rating, we totally understand! We’re certain we will soon have it. In the meantime, there were many Tamers who played on the Steam Deck during our Playtests and Steam Next Fest and gave a lot of positive feedback.

We are pretty happy with the previous patch, but it mostly affected the early game and early stages of progression. With this patch, however, we’re aiming at also getting a little control over the craziness when users start getting overpowered, with high-level techniques and more progression in the Skill Trees. We’ve noticed the early game is in a super good spot right now, but players scale too much and too quickly, so by the time bosses arrive they are unstoppable and bosses can’t even pose a realistic threat.

We’ve also increased the overall difficulty in Deniz, which was almost at the level of Cipanku, and made it much harder because players were reaching it with higher levels of progression. Almost all the enemies in Deniz are now stronger, and we also dedicated some time to improving Oceara to turn her into a much bigger threat with the reworked Sanative Rain.
Even with all the nerfs in the previous patch, Pigepic was still much stronger than the rest of the playable Tems, so we’ve revisited its whole moveset to further balance its damage output.

Last but not least, we’ve spent some time reworking the aimed techniques we currently have. Aimed techniques have been one of the most common complaints in user feedback and there are several solutions to make them feel better. To keep the strategy around aimed techniques intact, this time we opted to rework them so they are quicker to cast, notably reducing their cooldowns so you can better predict when a new technique is going to be used, and making it so failing one projectile doesn’t hurt that much because the next one will appear quicker.

Considering the initial player feedback and analytics for the Playtest, we believe it’s a bit too easy to progress through the main stages right now. We’ve tweaked multiple systems and stats to improve this feeling, especially making bosses stronger while slightly weakening all playable Tems. We’ve also increased the number of enemy Tems in Deniz to make it relatively more difficult than Cipanku, and made projectile-based enemies more menacing and notorious. Lastly, we’ve nerfed Pigepic’s synergies because they were simply too strong compared to other available synergies.

With all these changes we expect to improve the player experience and the difficulty feeling. Temtem: Swarm should feel like a challenging game that you master more and more through each run, especially by investing your time and earned Pansuns in the Skill Trees. A game like this with so many different interacting systems is very hard to fine-tune and perfect, so expect many more balance patches in the future.

Skill Tree’s economy has been reworked.
We’ve introduced Pansuns wallets for each Temtem, so now players will have a common wallet and another wallet for each Temtem.
Earned Pansuns in-game or with Kudos, will be sent to the common wallet, which can be spent on any Skill Tree.
However, refunding a Skill Tree, while still possible, will generate Pansuns linked to the Temtem, which you will only be able to use inside that Temtem Skill Tree.
When a new Temtem is captured, you’ll receive a bonus of Pansuns linked to that Temtem so you can start their Skill Tree with some progress.

Having the same currency for all Tems while also having the possibility of doing Skill Tree refunds, forced players to refund the full skill tree of their most advanced Temtem each time they captured a new one, in order to put all the Pansuns in the new Skill Tree. This effectively kills all the progression per Temtem and forces users to use this strategy in order to optimize the runs.
